basis: Metabolic encephalopathy with liver dysfunction; muscle atrophy 2/2 and CK elevation 3/6 support myopathy. Hearing loss and ASD each 2/6 omitted by cap.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the disorder. Constipation alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage; isolated cardiac reports do not establish common involvement.
Terminal spinal cord malformation herniates through a spinal dysraphic defect. Associated anorectal and urinary anomalies lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
Thyroid hormone transport disorder with euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia and possible goiter; no established extra-endocrine damage.
Infantile pulmonary disorder defined by persistent tachypnoea, within the infancy-specific interstitial lung disease spectrum.
Mature B-cell lymphoma establishes blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes. Breast origin adds no anatomical axis.
Metastatic malignancy occupies lymph nodes, which have no listed anatomical axis. This is not necessarily lymphoma or a blood-cell malignancy; primary origin is unspecified.
Nephronophthisis is the established core phenotype. Respiratory, retinal and CNS manifestations vary across this broad umbrella; frequencies supporting additional axes are unavailable.
Developmental cerebellar disorder; strabismus affects 3/4 patients. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; minor digit anomalies do not establish locomotor damage.
Coenzyme A metabolic defect causes neurodegeneration. Retinal dystrophy and optic pallor occur in 30-79%; dysphagia and stiffness reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Developmental disability and congenital heart defects define syndrome. Skeletal involvement includes hypermobility 5/6; optic nerve hypoplasia 2/6 and visual impairment 30-79%.
Congenital absence of part of an ocular structure; syndromic associations do not apply across the umbrella.
Glucose metabolism defect with hepatic glycogen storage. Renal storage causes common tubulopathy and hyperfiltration (>30%); stones and other separately diagnosed complications excluded.
Autoimmune neuromuscular junction disease with thymic hyperplasia. Weakness arises from impaired neuromuscular transmission rather than primary muscle injury.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy with developmental and central motor abnormalities; all established functional involvement is neurologic.
Germinoma arises within the CNS. Endocrine and visual consequences depend on tumour location and are not established as common across this umbrella.
Developmental dental enamel injury from excess fluoride. Teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis; skeletal fluorosis is a separate condition.
Chromaffin neuroendocrine tumour; catecholamine-mediated hypertension occurs in most patients (~60-80%). Severe cardiomyopathy and vascular events are minority complications.
Defined by partial or complete hearing loss. Central and syndromic subtypes do not justify additional axes across the umbrella.
Inherited CNS hypomyelination and neurodegeneration. Hearing loss and blindness are reported at 1-4%; respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct common pulmonary injury.
GPI-anchor metabolic disorder with intellectual disability. Phalangeal shortening 2/2; strabismus 2/3. Enteric anomalies, hearing loss and ASD each 1/2 omitted by cap.
Acute gallbladder inflammation; gallbladder belongs to hepatic axis. Inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Severe thyrotoxicosis; cardiac failure/atrial arrhythmia (~30-40%) and toxic encephalopathy (~50% or more) are major manifestations. Fever and simple tachycardia alone are excluded.
Metabolic defect of bone and tooth mineralization. Pulmonary disease and B6-responsive seizures concentrate in severe early-onset forms; supplied frequencies do not represent the whole umbrella.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; optic disc pallor and retinal vessel attenuation each reported in 1/2 support ocular involvement. Cerebral visual impairment remains neurologic.
